title: Selective Service chief: Russians moving agents through Orthodox churches
summary: Peter Levenda tells of Selective Service chief: Russians moving agents through Orthodox churches, about 1968 at Selective Service headquarters, New York City, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Selective Service headquarters, New York City

tellings.quote: he says the Russians have been moving agents into the United States through the Orthodox churches
The other church was the one on 97th Street and Fifth and that was the Russian church that owed allegiance to Moscow. That's the one they were running agents through.
tellings.difference: Names the specific church at 97th Street and Fifth Avenue, loyal to Moscow, and tells it firsthand rather than from the Selective Service chief.
tellings.link_reason: This tells the same claim as telling 1, that Russian agents were run through an Orthodox church, now pinned to the Moscow-aligned church.

plain: A writer named Peter Levenda says that around 1968 the head of the Selective Service in New York, the US office that ran the military draft, told him the Russians were sneaking spies into the United States through Orthodox churches. In another telling Levenda speaks as if from his own knowledge and names the church: a Russian church at 97th Street and Fifth Avenue in Manhattan that he says was loyal to Moscow. If true, it would mean Soviet spies were using a place of worship as cover in the middle of New York.
